correctness.rationale: The minimal DFA has r+s+1 reachable pairwise distinguishable states; suffix length r+s-j separates states i<j. For every input, c=max(r-#zeros,0) and capped ones-after-the-threshold-zero counts t_c,...,t_r determine each state image. Monotonicity is forced by threshold order. The map from signatures to transformations is injective (image of 0 determines c, image of i gives t_i) and surjective (alternating zero/one blocks realize arbitrary monotone tuples). Stars and bars plus hockey-stick gives binom(r+s+2,r+1)-1 including identity. Any nonempty word moves either state 0 (if any zero) or state r (if all ones), removing exactly one for the semigroup. Finite verifier independently constructs monoid closure and all normal-form maps for 36 parameter pairs, additional exhaustive representatives and word membership cases; the proof is uniform, not dependent on these finite tests.

value.rationale: The syntactic monoid is a natural automata-theoretic complexity invariant for principal shuffle ideals, elementary building blocks of piecewise-testable languages. The exact two-parameter theorem completely classifies the reachable transformations, in contrast with the known linear size of the canonical DFA. The balanced exponential-versus-linear gap is structural and makes a genuinely nontrivial exact all-parameter census; it is neither a small parameter increment nor a formal renaming of DFA state complexity.
